messages.subject: [amelia] Missing Data at Multiple Levels in a Nested Dataset
messages.subject_clean: [amelia] Missing Data at Multiple Levels in a Nested Dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hello Amelia User Community,
I have a question about imputing in multi-level data.

After reading older documentation, it seems that is possible to impute
nested data using the "cs" argument. I wonder, however, whether it is
possible to impute data missing at multiple levels. In my data set , for
example, I have children nested in classrooms. I have both children and
classrooms level variables, and there is missingness in both the child and
classroom level variables. As such, I need to impute at both levels. Is
this possible? I would hope for 10-20 data sets in which any value imputed
for a variable missing at the classroom level would take on the same value
for all children in that class.  Can Amelia do this? If so, how?

When I try using the cs="clustervar" option, the model does not converge.

Thanks so much,

Celia Gomez

-- 
*Celia Gomez*
*Doctoral Student*
*Human Development and Education*
*Harvard Graduate School of Education*

messages.subject: [amelia] problem installing Amelia View
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jenifer,

You can try to update Amelia to its latest version by opening up R and
typing the following command:

    install.packages("Amelia", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")

Then AmeliaView should open, either through the icon or by typing the
following commands in R:

    library(Amelia)
    AmeliaView()

Hope that helps!

Cheers,
matt.

~~~~~~~~~~~
Matthew Blackwell
Assistant Professor of Political Science
University of Rochester
url: http://www.mattblackwell.org
